item.description:
'Middle East situation could escalate rapidly': US urges citizens to exercise caution

The US government has told its citizens currently in the Middle East that the security environment remains "complex with the potential for unforeseen escalation", urging them to  exercise heightened vigilance.

In a statement, the state department asked Americans to also be aware of potential flight cancellations, airspace closures, and travel disruptions.

In separate travel alerts for Iraq, Bahrain, Oman, Saudi Arabia, Iran, Qatar, Lebanon, Kuwait and Jordan, US diplomatic missions in the nine countries said the security environment in the Middle East poses “the risk of flight cancellations, airspace closures and travel disruptions as regional tensions rise”.

"Iranian-supported Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including civilian airports. This military conflict has the potential to escalate rapidly. Americans outside the Middle East should seriously reconsider travel to and through the region," the alert said.

The alerts warned that Iran and groups supportive of Tehran could target US interests overseas or locations associated with Americans.

US citizens were advised to monitor airline and airport operations, avoid demonstrations and large gatherings and follow instructions from local authorities.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Former Syrian general who led attacks on rebels during civil war arrested
item.description:
Former Syrian general who led attacks on rebels during civil war arrested

Syrian authorities have arrested a general who served under the rule of ousted president Bashar al-Assad, saying he led operations against formerly rebel-held areas during the country's 13-year civil war.

In a statement, security forces announced "the arrest of former Major General Ahmed Mohammad Ismail, a high-ranking commander in the Republican Guard of the former regime's army".

Military records indicate that "he began his service as a platoon commander, then served as a company commander in the 2nd Battalion of the 101st Airborne Regiment. He was subsequently promoted, at the beginning of 2016, to Chief of Operations of the same regiment, and directly participated in commanding military assaults on the cities of Aleppo and Daraa, as well as on Eastern Ghouta."

Located near Damascus, Eastern Ghouta was a rebel stronghold during the civil war until 2018, and the site of a major chemical attack five years prior.

US intelligence says more than 1,000 people were killed with sarin nerve gas in the suburb of the Syrian capital Damascus, in 2013 during Syria's civil war.

The attack was attributed to the Syrian government under the rule of Bashar al-Assad, who was toppled in late 2024. The government at the time denied involvement and blamed rebels.

Report by AFP

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] West Bank: Eight Palestinians detained, settlers damage ambulance
item.description:
West Bank: Eight Palestinians detained, settlers damage ambulance

Eight Palestinians were detained, while several others suffered suffocation caused by a pepper spray attack by Israeli settlers, in the occupied West Bank. Here is an account of some of attacks and raids by Israeli forces and settlers reported by the Palestinian news agency Wafa:

Eight detained: Anti-settler activist Osama Makhamreh told Wafa that eight Palestinians were detained from the village of Ad-Deqaiqa, in the Masafer Yatta area south of Hebron, following an attack by Israeli settlers on Palestinians and their attempt to steal livestock.

He named the detained persons as Nasser Ahmad Nasser al-Najadeh, Abdul Rahman Mohammad al-Najadeh, Suleiman Mahmoud Kaabneh, Mohammad Suleiman al-Najadeh, Yousef Ahmad Mohammad Kaabneh, Mohammad Raad Amer, Odeh Salem al-Najadeh and his son Salem.

*Water supply cut: Settlers cut the main water line supplying the village, depriving around 700 residents of water.

*Solidarity activists attacked: In a separate incident, colonists attacked the home of Khairy Abu Tuffah in Khallet al-Hummus, south of Yatta, assaulting his family and foreign solidarity activists.

*Thirty guava trees cut: Settlers cut down 30 guava trees in the village of Khirbet Firasin near the town of Ya'bad, west of Jenin. The trees were owned by local Palestinian farmer Khaled Mohammad Amarnah.

*Attack near Ramallah outskirts: Israeli settlers, under the protection of Israeli forces, attacked the outskirts of Abu Falah village, northeast of Ramallah, on Saturday evening, while Israeli forces raided a commercial shop.

*Settlers use pepper spray: Several Palestinians suffered suffocation on Saturday evening after Israeli settlers attacked them with pepper spray near the entrance to al-Mughayyir village, northeast of Ramallah, head of the al-Mughayyir village council Amin Abu Alia told Wafa.

* Ambullance targeted: The settlers also targeted an ambulance belonging to the al-Mughayyir village council as it was heading to provide medical assistance to the injured Palestinians, causing material damage to the vehicle.

Abu Alia added that Israeli forces raided the village several times since last night, searching several homes, ransacking and damaging their contents, and assaulting several Palestinians.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Ed Sheeran says what is happening in Gaza is 'catastrophic, unjustifiable'
item.description:
Ed Sheeran says what is happening in Gaza is 'catastrophic, unjustifiable'

Pop Star Ed Sheeran has said what is happening in Gaza is “catastrophic and unjustifiable and disproportionate” as he opened his solo concert in the US city of Philadelphia.

Sheeran also said he was “appalled by the conflict between Israel and Palestine,” describing the suffering caused by the war as a “human tragedy,” while explaining that he has generally sought to keep his concerts focused on “unity, joy, escapism, love” rather than his own political views.

It was Sheeran's first show since he dropped US rapper Macklemore from his US tour after Macklemore called for a “Free Palestine”. Sheeran said he could not keep Macklemore after stadium owners refused to let him perform.

Sheeran drew flak for the move and his opening acts and his own band have quit the tour in solidarity with Macklemore.

“I have tried in my career not to be a political commentator of any kind, because I want my music and shows to be about unity, not division,” he said.

“But this is a humanitarian issue, and I cannot hide how I feel about it anymore. What happened in Israel and at the Nome Museum Festival on 7 Oct was horrific and compounded centuries of Jewish pain," he said.

"What is happening in Gaza is catastrophic and unjustifiable, and disproportionate. Our hearts can be broken by the scale of devastation and loss of civilians’s lives, children’s lives and the systemic injustice we’re seeing unfold in the West Bank cannot be overlooked.”

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Poll: US Jewish voters concerned Netanyahu policies fueling antisemitism
item.description:
Poll: US Jewish voters concerned Netanyahu policies fueling antisemitism

A majority of American Jewish voters say they are deeply concerned that Israel’s actions under Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have contributed to rising antisemitism and anti-Israel sentiment in the United States, even as an overwhelming majority continue to identify as pro-Israel, according to a new poll released this week.

The survey, conducted by the Mellman Group for the Jewish Electorate Institute and published Thursday, found that 56 percent of respondents had a “great deal” of concern that “Israel’s actions under Netanyahu have increased antisemitism and anti-Israel sentiment in the US”.

The view varied sharply by political affiliation, with 65 percent of Jewish Democrats expressing a high level of concern, compared with 46 percent of independents and 34 percent of Republicans.

Other Findings:

*Eighty-six percent of those surveyed described themselves as pro-Israel, while 65 percent of them said they were pro-Israel while critical of some or many Israeli government policies. 

*Seventy-one percent viewed Israel favourably, compared with 25 percent who viewed it unfavourably.

*Sixty-one percent viewed Netanyahu unfavourably and 34 percent favourably; 67 percent wanted to see him replaced in Israel’s upcoming election.

US military aid

Fifty-two percent favoured either cutting or ending the aid to Israel, including 36 percent who supported reducing it and 17 percent who favoured eliminating the $3.3 billion in military assistance. Forty percent wanted funding maintained at its current level.

Views of AIPAC and primary spending

Fifty-one percent said they had heard at least something about pro-Israel involvement in this year’s primary races, up from 38 percent in March. Thirty-nine percent supported such activity, while 35 percent opposed it and 26 percent were unsure.

Forty-two percent viewed the organisation favourably and 35 percent unfavourably, with 24 percent unsure.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Baghaei says attending UNGA meet Iran's right, not favour granted by US
item.description:
Baghaei says attending UNGA meet Iran's right, not favour granted by US

 Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson, Esmaeil Baghaei has said that Iran will not abandon its right to be present in the UN General Assembly, stressing that attending the UN meeting is not a privilege given by Washington, according to IRNA.

Speaking in a televised programme, Baghaei said that being in New York held absolutely no charm for Iranian representatives, but it was a "trench that must not be abandoned".

He said participating in the UN General Assembly was a legal right rather than a favour from others, as Iran was one of the 50 founding member states of the UN.

Baghaei said that the country had a duty to attend the most important international event to make the rights of the Iranian people heard by the world.

He added that the US "used every tool to prevent the Iranian delegation’s participation, ranging from derogatory remarks and media propaganda to abusing its commitments as the host government by creating delays or refusing to issue visas for several delegation members", IRNA reported.

item.description:
Six French Islamic State suspects to stand trial in Iraq

Six French nationals are due to stand trial in Iraq on Sunday, as the country assumes responsibility for prosecuting thousands of suspected Islamic State group members.

Iraq's prisons, already packed with IS suspects, have received thousands more detainees transferred since last year from neighbouring Syria. 

An Iraqi judicial source told AFP on Thursday that six French nationals were scheduled to stand trial on Sunday.

Their identities remain unclear, but they are part of a group of 47 French citizens transferred from Syria last year.

The larger group includes Adrien Guihal, who claimed responsibility for the 2016 Nice attack for IS.

Report by AFP

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] West Bank families led by women face greater displacement risks, OCHA says
item.description:
West Bank families led by women face greater displacement risks, OCHA says

Due to surging Israeli settler violence, West Bank families headed by women are more likely to be displaced and more likely to have chronic illness among household members compared with those headed by men, according to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA).

The agency estimates that some 83,000 households (one in eight families in the West Bank) are headed by women.

Nearly nine in 10 women interviewed who are heads of their households stated that checkpoints make travel feel unsafe, and more than half said movement restrictions are blocking access to their livelihoods.

A UN Women’s analysis of a survey, among women who are formally recognised as household heads, notes that 82 per cent are responsible for managing household income, 77 per cent are responsible for childcare 75 per cent make all decisions about household members’ safety and 65 per cent handle aid registration alone.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Trump cuts short weekend at Camp David, returns to White House
item.description:
Trump cuts short weekend at Camp David, returns to White House

US President Donald Trump cut short a weekend at Camp David to return unexpectedly to the White House on Saturday, as tensions rose in the Middle East.

There was no explanation from the administration why Trump was no longer returning on Sunday from Camp David, a secluded presidential complex in rural Maryland, as had been previously announced.

However, it is not uncommon for White House travel to change on weekends, including for weather reasons. Forecasts showed rain and thunderstorms in the hilly Camp David area on Sunday.

The change in plan came as the Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said on Saturday that the Iran-backed group fired a ballistic missile at Riyadh at dawn, after a fire broke out near the Saudi capital's international airport.

The State Department and a string of US embassies issued security alerts to Americans.

The alerts cited "the potential for unforeseen escalation" and noted that "Iranian-supported Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including civilian airports."

Report by AFP

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] 'Zionism=racism': Protest held outside Ed Sheeran's Philadelphia concert
item.description:
'Zionism=racism': Protest held outside Ed Sheeran's Philadelphia concert

Dozens of Palestinian supporters demonstrated outside Ed Sheeran concert in Philadelphia, denouncing promoters’s decision to drop US rapper Macklemore over his “Free Palestine” calls.

Carrying Palestinian flags, and banners with messages that read “Gaza: Aid in, soldiers out” and “Zionism=racism=terrorism”, the protesters criticised Sheeran for continuing the tour.

Adi Chattopadhyay, a spokesperson for the organisers of the protest, told Reuters that the demonstrators had gathered to call attention to Macklemore’s message and to talk “about the conditions on the ground in Gaza” and “the fact that the genocide is very much still ongoing”.

The 35-year-old pop icon kicked off the stage by saying what is happening in Gaza is "catastrophic and unjustifiable and disproportionate". 

Sheeran had reportedly said that stadium owners refused to allow Macklemore to perform over his Palestine remarks. 

In solidarity with Macklemore, Sheeran’s opening acts and members of his band later quit the US tour.

Israeli forces detain 27 Palestinians in raid on West Bank village, Wafa reports

Israeli forces have detained at least 27 Palestinians in a raid on the village of al-Mughayyir, east of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, the Palestinian news agency Wafa reported.

Local sources told Wafa that Israeli infantry units were deployed throughout the village early on Sunday morning and its only entrance was closed. 

Soldiers then raided several homes, ransacked their contents, and stole cash and gold jewellery, the agency said.

The detainees are being held at the home of Shaher Sari Abu Alia, according to Wafa.

The search and arrest campaign in al-Mughayyir follows an attack by Israeli settlers and forces on Saturday, the agency added.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Iran says Hormuz will not reopen until US honours June agreement
item.description:
Iran says Hormuz will not reopen until US honours June agreement

Iran’s parliament speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said Sunday that the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until the United States fulfils its commitments under a June agreement and meets Tehran’s conditions.

Speaking in parliament, Ghalibaf said Iran had “explicitly conveyed its conditions to the opposing side through intermediaries”, according to Iran’s state broadcaster IRIB.

Reuters has previously reported that Tehran has tied the reopening of the strait to US commitments under the June memorandum, including lifting its blockade of Iranian ports, oil sanctions and other measures.

“The enemy is well aware that the path of deception and unilateral imposition is closed,” Qalibaf said, adding that there would be no return to negotiations or reopening of the waterway until Iran’s rights were recognised and US commitments fulfilled.

The Strait of Hormuz is a major route for global oil and gas shipments, and traffic through the waterway has remained sharply below pre-war levels amid the continuing tensions.
